newsitem.title: CANADA: Starbucks Vancouver labor deal ratified.
newsitem.headline: Starbucks Vancouver labor deal ratified.

text.p: Starbucks Corp. said on Tuesday that 110 unionized workers in Vancouver ratified the coffee retailer's first ever union accord, which includes a provision basing pay increases on merit rather than seniority.

Seattle-based Starbucks said in a statement that under the two-year contract deal struck last week, employees "do not get automatic incremental pay increases based on predetermined dates in a contract."
"Instead, performance, skills and abilities will be considered for an employee-partner at Starbucks to progress from the minimum hourly pay to the maximum."
The two-year contract raises unionized workers' pay to an hourly base rate of C$7.75 (US$5.56), from C$7 (US$5.11), with an hourly increase of C12 cents (8.8 cents US) on July 1, 1998.
The Canadian Auto Workers union, which represents the unionized workers in eight coffee bars and a bakery distribution centre in Vancouver, had demanded an hourly increase to C$10 (US$7.30).
Starbucks said non-union employees in its other British Columbia stores would get the same basic pay increase as the unionized stores.
The 1,100-outlet Starbucks chain has more than 1,400 non-union employees in 87 other stores in British Columbia.
